design_rationale:
WORKLOG — travel_protection_desk / task 1 (care). Written as the task was designed; every figure below
comes from the verification run recorded at the end.

[Step 0 — draw, asset ledger and claim]
scripts/draw_counts.py env/online_travel_agency/tasks/travel_protection_desk --task 1 printed
{"task": 1, "key": "online_travel_agency/travel_protection_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2,
"problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4]}. The tree therefore carries two prerequisite problems and the
three computations 6, 4 and 4 declared factors: 6 on the correction of the declared trip cost
(care_ext_declared_cost_correction), 4 on the re-rating (care_ext_premium_rerating) and 4 on the release
of cover (care_ext_cover_release_return).
Already occupied by task 0: the claims half of the charter — care_subrogation, care_claim_filing,
care_claim_settlement and care_agg_benefit_coordination, with the three tools book_benefit_recovery,
file_benefit_claim and release_claim_payment. This task claims the disjoint half: care_policy_amendment,
care_premium_rating and care_free_look (with care_midterm_cancellation as input lineage), and its own
three tools. No policy and no tool is shared with task 0, and with these six the difficulty's extended
charter is complete.

Design thesis. Surface goal: 'I want to cancel the policy and get back whatever I am owed'. The scored
parameter is the premium returned. Between the goal and that figure the policy puts two problems the
customer never mentions: (a) the underwriting desk approved a correction of the declared trip cost weeks
ago and the certificate still carries the figure declared at quotation, and (b) the premium owed on the
corrected risk was never charged, so the record does not yet show what was collected for the cover.
Depth: surface goal -> the release rule -> its prerequisite sentence -> the premium record -> the
re-rating rule -> its own prerequisite sentence -> the certificate and the approved request -> the
operator's ledger. Breadth at the correction itself: the operator's record and ledger (what the holiday
cost, what counts as prepaid, what came back, what was settled in credit, the size of the party) and the
carrier's record (flights bought apart from the holiday).

[Base-invariant card]
care_insured_amend is governed by care_policy_amendment, which carries one gate, upgrade_approved
(authorization): 'Cover is upgraded only when the underwriting desk has already recorded an approved
cover upgrade against this policy.' It is satisfied by care_policy_requests row REQ, request_type
cover_upgrade, request_status approved, decided 2026-09-08, correlated to the write by care_request_id,
which is the parameter the blueprint's action_bindings fix. The plan held permits an upgrade
(cover_upgrade_allowed true) and its upgrade window is 14 days from issue: the certificate was issued
2026-08-30 and the request was submitted 2026-09-05 and approved 2026-09-08, both inside the window;
a request submitted on 2026-09-14 would have fallen outside it. Base's other clauses are inherited: an
increase in the declared trip cost is accepted only up to the plan's ceiling (20000.00 here, and the
corrected figure of 8806.67 is far below it), and no amendment is accepted once the journey has begun or
a claim has been filed — the journey begins 2026-10-10 and the claim record is empty.
care_premium_adjustment is governed by care_premium_rating alone, which carries no structured gate, so it
enters as policy_scope with every clause inherited: the premium follows the declared particulars, the
loadings are added and never compounded, the minimum premium floor applies, the policy fee is charged
once and never returned, and a change after issue is charged pro rata over the remaining days of cover.
care_cancel and care_premium_refund are governed by care_free_look. Its one gate, inside_free_look, is a
time gate, and care_ext_cover_release_return supersedes the clause that carries it, declaring the
supersession sentence by sentence in overwrite: base handles only the case inside the free-look period
('A free-look cancellation is handled at the full refund only when frozen time is not after ... plus the
free-look period of the plan held.'), while the extended rule legislates the whole domain — the plan's
mid-term share after the period has run, nothing where a claim stands filed, and the plan's free-look
share otherwise. Because the gate's condition sentence is the superseded clause, it is retired and
care_free_look enters the contract as policy_scope. Its other clauses stay in force and are inherited —
among them that the policy fee is never returned and that the free-look and mid-term terms are never
combined — with one exception added in the round 2 rework recorded below: the clause "A returned premium
is raised against the premium lines that collected it, so a policy with several premium lines returns as
several refund lines." is superseded by this policy's second overwrite, which names the one line the
return is raised against. Two clauses of care_free_look are therefore retired and the remaining five are
inherited.
There is therefore no time-kind eligibility left on any of this task's three writes and
temporal_feasibility is [].

[Business-object card]
The target object of all three writes is the one travel protection policy in the traveller's name
(certificate TG9M551740, TripGuard Plus, standing issued). The correction is authorised by one approved
request, correlated by care_request_id. The re-rating is raised against the base premium line of that
policy, named by source_entry_id, and the returned premium against the same line, so both derived lines
carry a unique link to the line they answer rather than resting on the policy id alone. The holiday the
cover was bought alongside is identified by the package the certificate links to and, in the rules, by
the air booking that departs on the first date of the journey; the traveller's sister travels on the
same package but is not named on the certificate, which is exactly what the party share excludes.

[Problem-tree card]
root_problem: care_ext_cover_release_return (what the customer asks for).
edge 1: care_ext_cover_release_return <- care_ext_premium_rerating, kind value_input, gate
premium_ledger, form state. Prerequisite sentence, from the blocked policy's own rule: 'The premium
returned is fixed only after the policy's premium record carries the re-rating owed on every correction
of the certificate's declared particulars.' Four-point test: (1) 'only after' is the ordering connective;
(2) it waits on a record-visible state, a re-rating line standing on the premium record; (3) it names no
tool, policy id or code token; (4) its strength is hard and its scope is every correction of the declared
particulars, exactly the edge's condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about:
the re-rating action. Derivation: the sentence says the return waits on a re-rating standing on the
record; the premium record carries four lines raised at issue and one small correction and no re-rating;
the re-rating policy's rule is the one that charges the difference after a declared particular changes;
so the re-rating must be raised first. Unmet at the opening: no row of care_premium_entries carries
event_type care_premium_adjustment. Skipping it: the premium returned falls from 127.99 to 109.81.
edge 2: care_ext_premium_rerating <- care_ext_declared_cost_correction, kind value_input, gate
rated_premium, form state. Prerequisite sentence: 'The re-rating owed on a correction is worked out only
after the certificate carries the declared particulars the underwriting desk has approved for it.' Four
points: (1) 'only after'; (2) a record-visible state, the declared particulars standing on the
certificate; (3) no tool, id or code token; (4) hard, and scoped to what the desk has approved. Exactly
one write of this difficulty brings that state about: the correction action. Derivation: the sentence
says the re-rating waits on the certificate carrying the approved particulars; the certificate carries
7400.00 while an approved request stands against the policy; the correction policy's rule is the one that
corrects the declared trip cost; so the correction comes first. Unmet at the opening:
initial_state.care_policies.<policy>.trip_cost_usd = 7400.0 while care_policy_requests.<request> stands
approved. Skipping it: the re-rating computes 0.00 instead of 108.36, because the premium the certificate
rates to then equals the premium already collected.
Topological order: the correction, the re-rating, the release. The edges form a chain, so no two writes
are free to be reordered and order_uniqueness records the chain rather than a commuting pair.
value_input edges: 2 of 2, and max(n-1, 1) = 1 is required for n = 2.
user_scenario mentions no prerequisite: it never names the approved request, an upgrade, a correction of
the declared trip cost or a premium re-rating. The customer says only that she wants to cancel and get
back what she is owed; she volunteers that a first amount left her card and that she thinks something
small came back, which are the two premium lines standing at the opening and no part of either
prerequisite. The tool layer validates nothing: correct_declared_trip_cost_b35383d2 performs one
ctx.update of the declared trip cost, raise_premium_rerating_6e8395e4 one ctx.create of a premium line,
and release_cover_and_return_premium_07b45938 one ctx.update of the policy status with the returned
premium line the cancellation triggers; none of them reads a request, an order or a status, and none can
refuse on policy grounds.

[Factor card — care_ext_declared_cost_correction, 6 factors, result 8806.67]
holiday_cost_basis (method, cross-difficulty bundle, multi-source): tier taken — the package stands
confirmed and its ledger carries a final payment, so the cost of the holiday is the charges standing on
that ledger, 1800.00 + 7600.00 + 620.00 + 480.00 = 10500.00. Baseline (the price the package was quoted
at, 11400.00) gives 9406.67.
prepaid_scope (method, cross-difficulty bundle): tier taken — the final payment has been taken and no
cancellation penalty stands, so the whole 10500.00 counts as prepaid. Baseline (the charges other than
optional components, 9400.00) gives 8073.33.
returned_money_excluded (parameter, cross-difficulty bundle): tier taken — the ledger carries 350.00 paid
back and the package stands confirmed, so 350.00 is taken out. Baseline (nothing) gives 9040.00.
credit_settlement_excluded (parameter, cross-difficulty bundle): tier taken — a 300.00 future travel
credit was settled against the holiday and no credit stands open on the record, so 300.00 is taken out.
Baseline (nothing) gives 9006.67.
party_share (parameter, cross-difficulty bundle): tier taken — the party is three adults with no children
and the certificate names two travellers, so two thirds of the cost is counted. Baseline (the whole) gives
12090.00.
flights_bought_apart (parameter, cross-difficulty air): tier taken — the air booking departing on
2026-10-10 stands ticketed and the package's ledger carries no flight component, so the 2240.00 paid on it
is added. Baseline (nothing) gives 6566.67. The near-miss here is the 2160.00 fare line on that
booking: it is what the second tier would have counted had the booking stood held rather than ticketed,
while the tier taken counts the money paid on the booking, 2240.00. The tour's own ledger carries no
charge for flights of any kind - its two component charges are both excursions - so the condition that
the holiday's ledger carries no flight component is plain on the records rather than a question of how a
charge category is read.
Whole baseline: 10300.00, against gold 8806.67. The traveller's own asked-for figure, 11400.00, stands on
the approved request and is the trap for an agent who copies the request instead of working the prepaid
cost out.

[Factor card — care_ext_premium_rerating, 4 factors, result 108.36]
rate_applied_source (parameter): tier taken — the premium record carries both an age loading line and a
destination loading line, so the rate applied is the one the premium collected bears to the trip cost the
base premium line was rated on: 654.16 / 7400.00 = 0.0884. Baseline (the plan's base rate with the plan's
destination loading, 0.0816) gives 56.17.
collected_premium_scope (parameter): tier taken — the record carries a line returned and a base premium
line, so the premium collected is the lines charged and the re-ratings raised less the lines returned and
less the policy fee: 679.22 - 10.06 - 15.00 = 654.16. Baseline (the figure the policy record shows paid,
669.16) gives 110.85.
effective_day_anchor (method): tier taken — an approved request stands and the journey has not begun, so
the change takes effect from 2026-09-08, the day the desk approved it, giving 61 days still to run.
Baseline (the day the certificate was issued, 2026-08-30) gives 124.35.
cover_span_convention (method): tier taken — the certificate was issued before the first date of the
journey, so the days of cover bought run from 2026-08-30 to 2026-11-07, both counted: 70 days. Baseline
(the days of the journey, 29) gives 261.56.
Whole baseline: 119.39, against gold 108.36.

[Factor card — care_ext_cover_release_return, 4 factors, result 127.99]
collected_lines_scope (parameter): tier taken — the record carries a line already returned and a line
charged for the issue fee, so the premium collected is 679.22 + 108.36 - 10.06 - 15.00 = 762.52. Baseline
(the whole of the lines charged and the re-ratings raised together with the lines already returned,
777.52) gives 130.51.
share_allowed_by_plan (parameter, multi-source): tier taken — cover is given up 22 days after issue,
more than the plan's 14-day free-look period, and no claim stands filed, so the share returned is the
plan's mid-term share of 25 per cent. Baseline (the plan's free-look share, 100 per cent) gives 511.98.
cover_bought_convention (method): tier taken — the certificate was issued before the first date of the
journey, so the days of cover bought run from 2026-08-30 to 2026-11-07, both counted: 70. Baseline (the
days of the journey, 29) gives 308.95.
cover_remaining_convention (method): tier taken — the journey has not begun and has not ended, so the days
remaining run from the day after the cancellation to 2026-11-07, both counted: 47. Baseline (the whole of
the days of cover bought) gives 190.63.
Whole baseline: 777.52, against gold 127.99.
Multi-source over this task: holiday_cost_basis, prepaid_scope, returned_money_excluded,
credit_settlement_excluded, party_share, flights_bought_apart and share_allowed_by_plan each combine two
conditions over distinct evidence on every tier beyond the fall-through. Cross-difficulty: five factors
read the operator's package record and ledger and one reads the carrier's booking, and both products are
seeded for this customer.

[World — why each class of row exists]
customers: one profile; the caller states her name and mobile to be found and her date of birth and the
postal code on her card to be verified.
care_policies: the one policy, standing issued with the journey still ahead of it, its declared trip cost
still 7400.00 and its premium_paid_usd 669.16. Change the declared trip cost and the re-rating changes;
change the issue date and both day-count conventions change.
care_premium_entries: five lines — base premium 503.20 (6.8 per cent of 7400.00), age loading 50.32 (10
per cent of the base for a 44-year-old), destination loading 110.70 raised at 22 per cent in error, the
policy fee 15.00, and the 10.06 correction that brought the loading back to the plan's 20 per cent. They
are what makes collected_premium_scope and collected_lines_scope bite, and the correction line is the row
that puts the customer on their first tier rather than their second.
care_policy_requests: the approved cover upgrade of 2026-09-08, which is the authorisation the amendment
gate demands and the reason the certificate is out of date; its requested_trip_cost_usd of 11400.00 is the
figure the traveller asked for and is deliberately not the figure the rules produce.
bundle_packages / bundle_ledger_entries: the escorted tour with three adults, its deposit, the credit
settled against that deposit, two component charges, the final payment and the refund for the excursion
dropped. Remove the refund and the corrected cost rises by 233.33; remove the credit and it rises by
200.00; make the party two adults and it rises by 3283.33.
air_bookings / air_booking_events: the flights bought apart from the tour, ticketed, 2240.00 paid.
Remove them and the corrected cost falls to 6566.67.
Automatic clauses checked: the policy has not incepted, so no benefit runs and no claim can arise; the
free-look period has run, so no full refund is owed; no premium instalment falls due; the package's own
obligations (its balance) are the operator's and are already settled on its ledger. Nothing in the seed
lights an obligation this task does not discharge.

[Persona]
Delphine is tired, organised and businesslike, and reads from paperwork rather than memory. She
volunteers only the surface request and her name and mobile; the date of birth, the postal code, the
operator's reference, the party, the journey dates and the fact that the flights were bought separately
come only when asked. Every fact she states points at a seeded row. She insists, unprompted, that the
cancellation be confirmed by her rather than done for her, which is the hand-over the task turns on, and
she is explicit that the desk may put right anything on its own side. She has no figure in mind for what
she is owed and accepts what she is told, so no gold figure can be parroted from her. Her last reaction
answers the last gold action - the cancellation going through and the money coming back - and she asks
for nothing beyond it.

[Standard solution]
Find the profile and verify. Read the policy, the premium lines, the requests on the policy, the package
and its ledger, the air booking and its ledger, and the claim record (empty). Read the release rule and
find that the return waits on a re-rating standing on the premium record; read the re-rating rule and
find that it in turn waits on the certificate carrying the approved particulars. Correct the declared
trip cost to the prepaid cost of the journey the records show: 10500.00 of charges on the package, less
350.00 returned and 300.00 settled in credit, two thirds of it for the two insured of the party of three,
plus the 2240.00 prepaid for the flights bought apart, giving 8806.67. Raise the re-rating: the
certificate now rates to 778.51 at the 0.0884 the collected premium bears to the 7400.00 the base line was
rated on, against 654.16 collected, a difference of 124.35 taken over the 61 of 70 days of cover still to
run from the day the desk approved the correction, giving 108.36. Then hand the cancellation to the
policyholder: 762.52 collected, 47 of 70 days remaining, the plan's 25 per cent mid-term share, giving
127.99.

[Verification run]
Command: .venv/bin/python scratch/verify1.py (the handling-time evaluator built on
skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py).
  care_ext_declared_cost_correction result=8806.67 branches=33
    holiday_cost_basis 9406.67 | prepaid_scope 8073.33 | returned_money_excluded 9040.0 |
    credit_settlement_excluded 9006.67 | party_share 12090.0 | flights_bought_apart 6566.67 |
    BASELINE(all)=10300.0
  care_ext_premium_rerating result=108.36 history_rows=6 branches=11
    rate_applied_source 56.17 | collected_premium_scope 110.85 | effective_day_anchor 124.35 |
    cover_span_convention 261.56 | BASELINE(all)=119.39
  care_ext_cover_release_return result=127.99 history_rows=6 branches=9
    collected_lines_scope 130.51 | share_allowed_by_plan 511.98 | cover_bought_convention 308.95 |
    cover_remaining_convention 190.63 | BASELINE(all)=777.52
  prerequisite sensitivity: skipping the correction leaves the re-rating at 0.00 instead of 108.36;
    skipping the re-rating leaves the return at 109.81 instead of 127.99.
These are exactly the values carried in computations and in the gold arguments.

[Two-way sweep rule <-> compute]
Forward: every binding that reads the world or chooses quotes its rule sentence verbatim in
compute_basis — the six ladders of the correction, the four of the re-rating and the four of the release,
with their evidence bindings. Backward: every load-bearing sentence of each rule is claimed by a binding.
The correction rule's sentences map to holiday_cost, holiday_prepaid, holiday_returned,
holiday_settled_in_credit, insured_share, flights_apart, journey_prepaid and result (the ceiling and the
rounding). The re-rating rule's map to rate_applied, collected_premium, rated_premium,
premium_difference, effective_from, days_of_cover_bought, days_still_to_run and result. The release
rule's map to premium_ledger, share_returned, days_of_cover_bought, days_of_cover_remaining and result.
Sensitive words checked: 'the policy fee excepted' -> a charge_category filter; 'more than the plan's
free-look period after the day the certificate was issued' -> DAYS against P('free_look_days'); 'both
counted' / 'that last date not counted' -> the +1 and -1 in the day counts; 'never less than nothing' ->
MX(...,0); 'never above the plan's ceiling' -> MN with P('max_trip_cost_usd'); 'rounded to two decimal
places at that step' -> the RND inside rated_premium.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context]
Masking the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this worklog, and reading only the published prose,
the tool schemas, the rows the share tools return and the persona: the desk sees a policy standing issued
with an approved upgrade against it and a certificate still carrying the old figure; the release rule says
the return waits on the re-rating, the re-rating rule says it waits on the corrected particulars; the
package ledger gives the prepaid cost and the party, the carrier's record gives the flights bought apart.
That reading gives 8806.67, then 108.36, then 127.99, in that order and on that one policy. The only
candidate ambiguity - whether to take the traveller's asked-for 11400.00 - is closed by the correction
rule, which fixes the declared trip cost to the prepaid cost the records show and never to the figure
asked for.

[Closure]
care_ext_declared_cost_correction -> correct_declared_trip_cost_b35383d2 -> computations[0] step 11 ->
  the certificate carrying 8806.67;
care_ext_premium_rerating -> raise_premium_rerating_6e8395e4 -> computations[1] step 13 ->
  a premium adjustment line of 108.36 against the base premium line;
care_ext_cover_release_return -> release_cover_and_return_premium_07b45938 (owner user) ->
  computations[2] step 15 -> the policy standing cancelled with a returned premium line of -127.99.
charter_scope claims exactly those three policies and three tools, required_documents repeats them in
order, and together with task 0 the six extended policies of this difficulty are covered exactly once
each with no overlap. No handoff is called.

[Manual values gates — task 1, run after the per-task scripts went green]
Length, breadth and the hidden test: walked from 'cancel it and give me back what I am owed' to the
return through two prerequisite sentences in a chain; the breadth at the correction is the operator's
record and ledger and the carrier's booking, and deleting any of the six factors moves the number. One
problem of the tree is the customer's own write, and giving up cover is what the charter reserves to the
policyholder; she confirms it while she is on the line.
Need and simulator boundary: she states the object (her own policy), the timing (now), the authorisation
(the desk may tidy up its side, she confirms the cancellation herself) and that a write is wanted. She
never reads policy, never offers a figure and never names a prerequisite.
Opening chronology: the tour dates, the party, the separate flights and the two premium movements she
half-remembers all point at seeded rows; the correction, the re-rating and the return are things only
gold produces and she says nothing of them.
Base eligibility and the time anchor: the plan's free-look period is the term that decides the share -
issued 2026-08-30, period 14 days, so 2026-09-13 is the last day inside it and frozen_time 2026-09-21 is
outside; a cancellation confirmed on 2026-09-13 would have taken the plan's free-look share and the whole
premium instead. The upgrade window is checked the same way: 14 days from issue, the request submitted on
day 6 and approved on day 9, both inside. The base gate carrying the free-look boundary is superseded
clause by clause in overwrite, so it is not inherited as a gate; every other clause of care_free_look is.
Authoritative facts and the business object: the authority for the correction is the approved request
row, not the caller, and her own asked-for figure of 11400.00 is deliberately not the figure the rules
produce; both derived premium lines name the base premium line they answer.
Reachability and no real-world waits: the approval is dated 2026-09-08, the package ledger closed on
2026-09-12, and all three writes land under one frozen clock with nothing waiting on clearing or a future
date.
Prerequisite sentences: both pass the four-point test, both are state-form, and each state is brought
about by exactly one write of this difficulty.
rule/compute equivalence and honest labels: swept both ways; the four method factors are selection rules
and day-count conventions, the four parameter factors select amounts, a rate and a share.
Draft recomputation from the visible context: recorded above; it reaches 8806.67, 108.36 and 127.99, and
the only candidate ambiguity is closed by the correction rule.

[Round 2 rework — items answered by id; the source layer only, the documents to be re-rendered]

Item 1 / O8 / policy_kb 1.md note 7 / runtime 1.md observation 3 — `source_entry_id` was not
uniquely entailed. CLOSED IN THE RULE, and no scored value moved. Both writes take one premium line
while base care_free_look said "A returned premium is raised against the premium lines that
collected it, so a policy with several premium lines returns as several refund lines", the record
carries four charge lines, and the seed's own 10.06 correction is raised against the destination
loading line. Two changes: (a) care_ext_premium_rerating's rule now states "A re-rating is raised
against the line that carries the base premium of the certificate, because that is the line the whole
premium was rated from, and where the premium record carries no such line it is raised against the
earliest line charged on the policy; a loading line, the line charged for the issue fee and a line
raised to correct another line are never the line a re-rating is raised against." (b)
care_ext_cover_release_return's rule states the same in its own terms for the return, and the policy
now declares a second overwrite naming the base clause it supersedes, so the plural-lines reading is
retired on the extended side rather than left standing beside a single-line tool. The seed no longer
points elsewhere either: the three kinds the rule excludes are exactly the three kinds the record
carries besides the base premium line, and the 10.06 row's own attachment - a correction attaching to
the line it corrects - is named as one of them, so precedent and rule now agree that it is not the
line a return is raised against. That is recorded in the task's solvability_contract.seed_consistency as well, on the entry whose row is
that premium line, in its check field.
Nothing computed reads source_entry_id, so all three expected values, every factor baseline and both
baseline_result figures are unchanged (COMPUTE re-run green on the same numbers).

Item 2 / policy_kb 1.md note 6 / runtime 1.md observation 4 — the base/extended divergence this world
reaches. DECLARED. care_club_and_bundle_interaction's "Cover bought alongside an air booking or a
vacation package is rated on the same declared trip cost as that booking, and the two are corrected
together where the booking's price changes." read alone points at the package's 11400.00 where this
policy computes 8806.67, so by the test - evaluate the quantity this policy computes and base's
provision for the same quantity, once each, in the same world - it differs and must be declared. It
is now the overwrite on care_ext_declared_cost_correction, superseded by that policy's own opening
sentence ("the declared trip cost is corrected to the prepaid cost of the journey the records show,
and never above the plan's ceiling"), with care_club_and_bundle_interaction added to
base_policy_refs so the lineage is declared before it is superseded. Its other clauses - the club
discount, the mutual exclusivity with a corporate rate, the points accrual and the lapse rule - are
untouched and stay inherited.

Item 3 / policy_kb 1.md note 8 / runtime 1.md observation 1 — seed narrowness on `flight_component`.
CLOSED IN THE WORLD. The 480.00 component charge on the tour ledger was categorised `flight_upgrade`,
which on a category-name reading could be taken for "a flight component" and would move the corrected
declaration by 2240.00. It is now `excursion_component`, a second excursion beside the 620.00 one, so
the tour's ledger carries no charge for flights of any kind and the tier's condition is plain on the
records instead of resting on the document's prose. The rule, the ladder and the compute are
unchanged: `pkg_components` sums by event type and still totals 1100.00, `pkg_flight_components`
still totals nothing, and the corrected declaration is still 8806.67. The factor keeps its near-miss
in the 2160.00 fare line, which is what its second tier would have counted had the booking stood held
rather than ticketed.

runtime 1.md observation 2 — `requested_trip_cost_usd` 11400.0 on the approved request is an inviting
wrong answer. KEPT DELIBERATELY, and now closed twice over: the correction basis fixes the figure to
the prepaid cost the records show, and the declaration under item 2 retires the one base sentence that
could be read as endorsing the package price. It is the trap the computation is built around and no
rule reads the field.

runtime 1.md observation 5 — the request typed `cover_upgrade` against a trip-cost correction. NO
CHANGE. The gate whose condition must be satisfied is care_policy_amendment's "Cover is upgraded only
when the underwriting desk has already recorded an approved cover upgrade against this policy", so a
request of exactly that type is what makes the gate literally true; raising the declared cover is what
an upgrade of a trip-cost declaration is, the plan permits upgrades, and the request stands inside the
plan's 14-day upgrade window. The correction reads the request by its reference and never by its type.

user_scenario:
Delphine Marchetti is forty-four, a hospital pharmacist in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and she rings the travel protection desk late in the afternoon after a shift, sounding tired but organised, with a folder of paperwork in front of her. She opens by saying her name, Delphine Marchetti, and that the desk should have her on 7030558214, then explains that she took out travel insurance in August for a tour she is taking to Japan in October with her husband and her sister, and that her hospital has since put her on its own corporate travel cover for the trip. Because of that she wants to cancel the policy and get back whatever she is owed, and she says so in those words.

She is clear about what she wants done and by whom. She is content for the desk to put right anything on the policy that needs putting right at its end, and says so if the agent asks - "if there's tidying up to do on your side, do it" - but she says twice, unprompted, that she wants the cancellation itself confirmed by her, not done quietly on her behalf, because it is her contract. When the agent explains what she is confirming and passes it to her, she goes through with it once and immediately.

She keeps her paperwork close and reads from it only when asked. Her date of birth is 1982-04-17. The postal code on the card she paid with is 02139. She has the tour's own paperwork too, and if the agent asks for the operator's reference she reads out WL-PKG-55218. She does not know her policy number or certificate number and says the desk will have to find them. She has no idea what the premium came to in the end - she says a first amount left her card in August and thinks something small came back afterwards, but she would have to dig out the statement and would rather the desk read it off the record.

Asked about the trip itself, she says the tour leaves on the tenth of October and comes back on the seventh of November, that there are three adults on the booking and no children, and that she and her husband are the two named on the insurance, her sister having her own. If she is asked whether she has travelled yet or claimed anything, she says no to both, quite definitely: the trip has not started and nothing has ever been claimed on this policy. If she is asked whether the flights are part of the tour, she says no, they booked those separately in August and paid for them then.

She does not know what she is owed and says as much if the agent asks whether she has a figure in mind. When a figure is put to her she accepts it without checking, saying she has no way of working it out herself. If the agent tells her the cancellation has gone through and the money is on its way back to her card, she says that is exactly what she needed, thanks them and ends the call. She asks for no letter, no confirmation email and nothing else besides.

The base premium of 503.20 posted on the issue date: the plan's base rate of 6.8 per cent on the 7400.00 declared at quotation.

The age loading of 50.32 posted on the issue date: 10 per cent of the base premium, the plan's ladder percentage for a 44-year-old, added to the base premium and not compounded with the destination loading.

The destination loading of 110.70 posted on the issue date: raised at 22 per cent of the base premium, which is not the plan's own 20 per cent for the declared region, and corrected by the returned line below.
The policy fee of 15.00 posted on the issue date: the plan's flat issue fee, charged once per certificate and never returned.

The 10.06 returned on 2026-09-01 against the destination loading line, bringing that loading from the 110.70 first raised to the 100.64 the plan's 20 per cent gives on the base premium; the five lines together are the 669.16 the policy record shows paid. It is raised against the destination loading line because a line raised to correct another line attaches to the line it corrects, which is the one kind of attachment the re-rating and return rules exclude by name, so this row is no precedent for the line either of those writes is raised against.

Skipping the correction leaves the certificate at 7400.00, so the premium the certificate rates to is 654.16, exactly what was collected, and the scored re-rating falls from 108.36 to 0.00; the return then falls with it.
